headline: Ad pricing and user growth accelerate; outlook stays strong
summary_short: Reddit's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $804.9M (+61% y/y, +21% q/q) as global DAUq grew 18% to 130.3 million and ARPU jumped 36% to $6.18 on higher ad pricing; net income more than doubled y/y to $252.8M and Q3 revenue guidance of $860-870M implies growth holding near 47-49%.
summary_long: Revenue growth accelerated to 61% y/y (from ad pricing +~40% and impressions +~17%, per the release), with international revenue (+84% y/y) outgrowing the U.S. (+56% y/y). Gross margin expanded 50bp to 91.3% even as cost of revenue rose 53% on higher hosting usage, partly offset by hosting efficiencies. Operating income more than tripled y/y to $231.7M as revenue outgrew opex; R&D, sales & marketing and G&A all grew slower than revenue. Net income reached $252.8M (31% margin). Free cash flow was $260.7M. Reddit repurchased 1.5M shares for $235M during the quarter; cash and marketable securities stood at $2.8B. Management guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $860-870M (47-49% y/y growth) and Adjusted EBITDA to $385-395M (63-67% y/y growth).

drivers.explanation: Eighth consecutive quarter of over 60% revenue growth; management attributes it to ad pricing and impression growth, and DAUq growth driven by machine translation, marketing and product improvements.

Advertising revenue +64% y/y from ad prices up ~40% (better full-funnel ad performance, higher advertiser demand) and impressions up ~17% (ad load optimization, new placements, more users/engagement).
Increased hosting usage to support product enhancements and user growth, partially offset by lower hosting prices and hosting cost efficiencies.
Revenue (+61% y/y) grew far faster than total costs and expenses (+33% y/y), per the release's own revenue-vs-cost-growth framing.
Followed operating income's rise, plus other income up 19% y/y on higher interest earned from a larger invested cash/investments balance.

Q/q decline vs Q1 FY2026's $312.3M despite higher net income; not decomposed by the release for the sequential comparison (y/y comparison is explained: higher net income plus SBC and working-capital timing).
Operating cash flow of $262M plus $219.5M from investing (net securities maturities), partly offset by $244.1M used in financing, mainly $234.6M of share repurchases.
